title: Wallet: Don't backdate locktime rbf

traits.before: anti-fee-sniping (±100 blocks); a bumpfee replacement can get a lower nLockTime than the tx it replaces
traits.after: anti-fee-sniping (±100 blocks); a bumpfee replacement's nLockTime is never below the original's
traits.evidence: src/wallet/spend.cpp DiscourageFeeSniping: `if (rng_fast.randrange(10) == 0 && tx.nLockTime > minimum_height) { int range = std::min(100, int(block_height - minimum_height + 1)); ...}`; src/wallet/feebumper.cpp: `new_coin_control.m_minimum_locktime = tx->nLockTime;`

summary: Fee-bump replacements made by bumpfee no longer get an nLockTime lower than the transaction they replace, which the PR author measured as a rare (<2% of replacements) on-chain pattern that singles out Bitcoin Core and Electrum.
notes: Affects the bumpfee path only (CreateRateBumpTransaction). Normal sends are unchanged. If the chain is lagging, the locktime becomes the original's locktime instead of 0. Closes issue #26526.

title: wallet: deprecate replaceable argument from transaction (and psbt) creation (and modification) RPCs

traits.after: 0xFFFFFFFD (RBF); per-transaction opt-out needs -deprecatedrpc=bip125 (the -walletrbf=0 startup option still works)

summary: Users can no longer opt individual transactions out of RBF signalling, so fewer Core transactions should carry nSequence 0xFFFFFFFE.
notes: The default is unchanged. This only removes a per-tx option, so the effect is limited to users who used replaceable=false. A sibling PR that flipped the -walletrbf default to false (#35405, giving 0xFFFFFFFE by default) was closed after mailing-list feedback preferred keeping MAX-2. Draft #35442 still carries that stale commit; it was excluded because its own commits are test-only.

title: wallet: skip APS when no partial spend exists

traits.before: second coin-selection pass grouped by address always runs; its input set is used whenever its fee is <= the normal selection's (default -maxapsfee=0)
traits.after: the grouped pass runs only if the normal selection spends some but not all UTXOs of an address; otherwise the normal selection's inputs are kept
traits.evidence: src/wallet/spend.cpp CreateTransaction: `... && !coin_control.m_avoid_partial_spends && txr_ungrouped.has_partial_spend)`; master use_aps check at spend.cpp:1486 `txr_grouped->fee <= txr_ungrouped.fee + wallet.m_max_aps_fee`

summary: When the normal coin selection leaves no address partially spent, the wallet keeps that input set instead of sometimes switching to the address-grouped selection, which can change how many and which inputs a transaction has.
notes: Default send path. The on-chain effect is indirect (input count/selection) and probably small; the PR mainly fixes over-reporting of APS use (issue #25150).

title: wallet: allow skipping script paths

traits.before: signs and finalizes taproot script paths too; falls back to a script-path spend when no key-path signature is available
traits.after: opt-in keypath_only: no script-path signatures are added and the PSBT is not finalized without a key-path signature, so the tx only ever appears on chain as a key-path spend
traits.evidence: src/script/sign.cpp SignTaproot: `if (taproot_keypath_only) spenddata.scripts.clear();` ... `// Key path signing failed. In keypath-only mode, stop here ... if (taproot_keypath_only) return false;`

summary: Adds an option so taproot wallets with script-path fallbacks (e.g. MuSig2 2-of-2 with a timelocked backup) never broadcast a script-path spend by accident, keeping the spend a 64-byte key-path signature on chain.
notes: Opt-in: keypath_only option (default false) on send, sendall, walletcreatefundedpsbt, walletprocesspsbt and descriptorprocesspsbt. Only matters for taproot descriptors that have script leaves.

title: Silent Payments:  Sending (take 2)

traits.before: cannot pay BIP352 silent payment (sp1...) addresses
traits.after: pays sp addresses with a P2TR output derived from the input keys (BIP352)

traits.before: coin selection picks any spendable inputs
traits.after: for sp sends: at least one BIP352-eligible input (P2WPKH, P2TR key-path, P2SH-P2WPKH, compressed P2PKH) is forced into the selection, preferring confirmed coins; inputs of unknown witness version and external inputs are refused
traits.evidence: src/wallet/spend.cpp SelectCoinsForSilentPayments: `// Otherwise, preset an eligible coin (the anchor) and select again. Confirmed coins are tried first`; CheckSilentPaymentsInput: `... has an unknown witness version and cannot be used in a silent payments transaction`

summary: Lets the wallet send to silent payment addresses, creating BIP352-derived P2TR outputs and shaping the input set so that at least one eligible input is present.
notes: Opt-in: only when a recipient is an sp address. Also blocks sp sends that could not be fee-bumped safely (PSBT creation, add_to_wallet=false). Depends on #35301 (marked done in the PR body). Change type follows the existing 'matches payment' logic (recipient is P2TR).

title: Silent Payments: Receiving

traits.after: when paying an sp address from an sp wallet, change goes to a BIP352-derived silent-payment change output (P2TR)
traits.evidence: src/wallet/spend.cpp: `if (change_sp) { // Generate output for change too  sp_dests[sp_change_index] = *change_sp; }` and change prototype `GetScriptForDestination(WitnessV1Taproot())`

traits.before: cannot receive or spend silent payment outputs
traits.after: sp descriptor wallets scan for and spend BIP352 outputs (P2TR key path with tweaked keys)
traits.evidence: adds SilentPaymentsDescriptorScriptPubKeyMan (src/wallet/scriptpubkeyman.cpp) and an sp() descriptor (src/script/descriptor.cpp)

summary: Adds silent-payment receiving wallets, whose spends are P2TR key-path inputs and whose change on sp sends is itself a silent-payment P2TR output.
notes: Draft. Depends on #35301 and #35302; the diff is built against older sending code, so details may change. Opt-in: needs an sp descriptor wallet. The change output stays P2TR like the payment, so the observable change type barely moves.
